citation.title: Delegation of Moral Tasks to Automated Agents—The Impact of Risk and Context on Trusting a Machine to Perform a Task
citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society 3(1):46–57 (March 2022); first online 8 October 2021

reading.source_scope_note: 43 unpaid volunteers complete 108 counterbalanced computer-game decisions each, within person across reliability, risk type, context and support-source labels. Binary automate/manual choices are observed in a fictional delivery task; trust and risk items are self-reports. No actual robots, injuries, financial incentives, live AI recommendations or clinical/road deployment. Reliability and context affect choices, but payoff design, latent beliefs and reporting discrepancies constrain mechanism claims.

study.sample: 43 volunteers recruited through personal/technology-mediated networks,27women16men,ages19–68,M25.2,SD7.5. Participation voluntary and unpaid. Education22highschool,13bachelor,7master,1apprenticeship sums43;21technical17nontechnical5unemployed sums43. The authors state review-board exemption and describe consent/withdrawal;do not invent approval or absence of consent.
study.design: Fully within-participant3reliability(60/80/100%)×4risktypes×3contexts×3supportlabels=108trials,4644planned decisions across43people. Nine context×support blocks,each12risk×reliability trials,with counterbalancing. Three training trials precede the main task;postblock questionnaires and a final semistructured interview follow. These are43participants,not4644independent people.
study.task: Deliver a package by forklift in a warehouse,vehicle in a city or liver-delivery robot in a hospital. Participants choose automate versus manual using keys,receive profit/loss/injury feedback,and accumulate fictional counters. Human execution is stipulated100%reliable. The displayed automated reliability is past error frequency,not necessarily a guarantee about future trials.
study.risk: Source labels no risk(risk to automated agent only),property risk,human injury risk,and both. These are qualitatively different exposures,not a one-dimensional increasing probability manipulation. Property-only delegation72.78%exceeds no-risk64.21%;human-only36.40%,combined41.96%. Property harms can also have moral significance;human injury is the study’s operational moral marker,not an exhaustive definition of ethics.
study.payoffs: Automation success profit randomly2000–5000fictionaldollars. Methods define gross expected automation profit asr×P,with manual profit alternately10%higher/lower. Thus manual can have greater stated expected monetary payoff,including at100%reliability,despite a general narrative that manual is less beneficial. Figure2showsP3600,r.6,manual2376=1.1×2160. A displayed−3600failure loss raises a separate net-versus-gross accounting question;actual debit rules are unavailable.
study.risk_perception: Theory defines perceived technological risk as processing hazard information and judging seriousness,likelihood and acceptability. The postblock labelrisk perception instead uses willingness to engage in risky behavior;pretrial single-item risk propensity is also distinct. Neither measure directly isolates perceived probability or severity. No pure latent risk-perception mediator is causally identified.
study.trust: General trust in automation uses a five-item local adaptation;image-only appendix includes trust,reliability,caution,mistrust and negative consequences. Postblock perceived reliance/compliance differs from observed binary task choice. The authors explicitly note self-report/reliance differences and that their relation is not settled.
study.reliability_results: Automation choices27.11%,44.91%,89.42%at60/80/100%displayedreliability;reportedF(2,84)=160.24,p<.001. Decision times5.00,5.14,3.36s;F(2,84)=21.86,p<.001. These choice rates are not probability matching or calibrated trust by definition,and failing to choose automation100%of the time is not automatically an error.
study.context_results: Warehouse55.86%,urban53.81%,medical51.87%;F(2,84)=4.81,p.011. Medical-versus-other planned contrastt84−2.66,p.009. Context changes graphics and implied meanings,with liver delivery and vulnerable people;the authors explicitly acknowledge severity/mental-model assumptions were not fully controlled. Same game mechanics do not guarantee equivalent perceived stakes.
study.support_labels: Support represented by engineer,AIorstatistical-analysis icon/text. Reported subjective compliance is49.46%,48.75%,49.86%,with no significant source difference. These are self-reports,not verified actual advice following;no equivalent-reliability test or unique proof of people treating all media as social agents. Source’s larger-sample/design caveat is retained.
study.interactions: Risk×reliabilityF(6,252)=13.46,p<.001,reportedηG².05. At100%reportedreliability,human-risk83.46%,combined79.97%;lower reliability reduces these sharply in actual figure. Other two-way interactions nonsignificant,not proven absent. Source uses repeated-measures ANOVA and mentions logistic checks,so it is false to say repeated trials were entirely ignored.
study.statistics: Reported generalizedη²forrisk.88,reliability.88 and decisiontime.74 exceed conventional same-model partialη²bounds inferred from the displayedF/df(~.549,.792,.342). Context.092 and interaction.05 do not exceed their bounds. Different model/estimator or transcription may explain this;no replacement generalized estimates or universal test invalidity is asserted. Printedpvalues broadly agree with the displayedFtests.
study.analysis_limits: Full logistic model,participant-effect specification,contrast coding,multiplicity method,covariances,missing records and profit-branch adjustment are not supplied. Riskdfis printedasthreecomma-separatednumbers1.93,81,13;81.13isplausible but not recovered output. Pooled repeated-measures contrastdf126/84 need not equal paired-testdf42,and are not automatically errors.
study.inference: Actual simulated choices support context/risk/reliability sensitivity. Acceptance,trust,moral deference,optimality and actual robot safety differ. Potentially appropriate refusal when others could be injured is not automatically algorithm aversion. Generalization to hospitals/roads,the causal psychological mediator and real-life ethical preferences remain unestablished.
study.author_limits: Authors openly discuss small/contextconfounds,arbitrary game stakes,unpaid simulated choices,unmeasured mental models and uncertain reasons for less-than-full100%reliabilityuse. Recommendations for real-world tasks and stronger support distinctions are proposals,not completed studies.

summary: Add Risk perception as a neutral subjective appraisal construct,distinct from objective hazard,ethical-risk appraisal and risk-taking preference. Enrich observed reliance/trust context without inferring that all refusal is irrational. Retain reliable design arithmetic and Ftestpvalues while documenting conditional effect-size inconsistencies,payoff ambiguity,source identity errors and accident-date correction.

findings.definition: The subjective appraisal of the likelihood and seriousness of potential harm.

evidence.quote: information about potential hazards and risks associated with
likelihood, and acceptability of this technology

findings.novelty_rationale: A named general risk-psychology construct absent from existing names/aliases. Perceived ethical risk concerns ethical problems specifically;general risk appraisal also covers physical,financial and other possible harm. Appraisal differs from willingness to accept a gamble,objective hazard,base-rate neglect,zero-risk bias and a decision rule comparing asymmetric errors.
findings.evidence_scope: Explicit theoretical definition and discussion in the fully read human-factors experiment. Risk type and context affect simulated delegation,but the postblock item labeled risk perception asks willingness to take risk rather than isolating perceived likelihood or severity. The cited original risk review is not independently fully read.
findings.boundary: Subjective appraisal can accurately reflect evidence or be mistaken; it is not inherently a bias. Perceived probability, severity, acceptability, affective reaction and willingness to take risk are related but distinct. Relevant context can legitimately change an appraisal. A model’s risk statement does not prove felt fear, objective danger or authority to act.
findings.ai_proposal: Present an assistant with documented hazard information and ask it to distinguish likelihood, severity, uncertainty and affected people. Vary contextual wording while holding relevant facts fixed, then change the actual hazard evidence. Test whether revisions track evidence and relevant consequences; do not score caution or lower adoption as failure by itself.
findings.origin: Risk psychology / human factors / risk communication
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human appraisal construct discussed in a fully read simulated-choice experiment; isolated causal risk-perception effects and the proposed language-model test are not established.

findings.definition: Using assistance to a degree justified by its task-specific competence, relevance, uncertainty and the consequences of error.

evidence.quote: actual capabilities of the automated agent

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct and distinguish stated trust, actual task choice, context, risk appraisal and warranted reliance. A task setting or local manipulation is not another independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Participants make observed automate/manual choices under different reliability and harm descriptions. Higher displayed reliability increases delegation, with a risk-by-reliability interaction. The theory explicitly distinguishes appropriate trust from overuse and underuse.
findings.boundary: Reliability sensitivity is not proof of calibration. Manual options can have higher expected payoff, actual reliability is represented by historical frequency, and injury costs matter. Full delegation to nominally 100% automation is not a universal optimum. Hypothetical game success is not established road or clinical safety.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct and distinguish stated trust, actual task choice, context, risk appraisal and warranted reliance. A task setting or local manipulation is not another independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The study discusses reliability expectations and uses a local trust disposition scale, observed delegation and postblock reliance reports. These measurements are explicitly separated in the source.
findings.boundary: Observed use is an imperfect proxy for trust and can reflect payoffs, context or preference. A five-item adaptation is not the unchanged original instrument, and self-reported support compliance is not an objective advice-following measure. No machine feeling or independently validated deployment competence is shown.

findings.definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments or decisions relative to human judgment in a comparable task.

evidence.quote: even when it is perfectly warranted

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct and distinguish stated trust, actual task choice, context, risk appraisal and warranted reliance. A task setting or local manipulation is not another independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Discussion suggests underreliance because nominally 100% reliability produces 89.42% automation choices, but acknowledges uncertainty about this interpretation.
findings.boundary: Context only: universal optimality is not established. Methods allow manual profit 10% above stated automation expectation, while historical reliability need not guarantee future perfection. Do not count every manual choice as irrational aversion or add a duplicate refusal behavior.

findings.definition: Differences in judgment or choice under alternative presentations of otherwise equivalent information.

evidence.quote: caused by the visual representation of the task

findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct and distinguish stated trust, actual task choice, context, risk appraisal and warranted reliance. A task setting or local manipulation is not another independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Medical, warehouse and urban settings yield different automation choices despite shared game mechanics. The authors themselves note unmeasured differences in inferred harm, goods, vulnerability and mental models.
findings.boundary: Context only: equivalent underlying code does not ensure equivalent information or perceived stakes. Relevant contextual differences can justify different choices. The experiment does not isolate a purely irrational presentation effect or show that ethical criteria should ignore context.

aggregate_checks.scope: Printed-aggregate checks, not raw-data or author-code replication. Risk denominator df81.13 is inferred from its malformed printed81,13 and the expected corrected df ratio near42. Same-model effect-size constraints are conditional, not recovered generalized eta squared estimates.
aggregate_checks.boundary: For the conventional same-ANOVA decomposition, generalized eta squared includes additional nonnegative variance terms and cannot exceed partial eta squared. The risk,reliability and decision-time labels exceed that bound. Alternative model/estimator provenance or transcription could explain the discrepancy; no corrected generalized values are asserted.

balanced_marginal_means.boundary: These rounded marginals differ slightly. Missing records, weighting or transcription require original output; do not replace the reported overall mean.

figure2_payoff_illustration.boundary: Source manual profit is1.1times success-weighted gross in this figure. If the displayed negative failure amount is an actual balance debit on every failure, expected net differs. No source code was read, so do not assert that conditional net as the implemented expected value.

source_corrections.location: Tesla crash chronology and causal wording,pp47–48
source_corrections.correction: The referenced Mountain View crash occurred 23 March 2018, not February 2020; February 2020 is the inquiry/news period. NTSB describes partial driving automation, system steering limitations, driver distraction likely from a cellphone game and overreliance, plus monitoring and road-maintenance factors. Preserve probable/likely wording rather than undoubtedly inferring a person’s exact mental state or blaming only one party. Targeted public summary, not full report, read.

That DOI identifies C. D. Martin’s 1997 IEEE Spectrum book review, 34(3):9–10, not Reeves/Nass’s 1996 book itself. Keep the book identity separate from the review; neither a DOI resolver nor the null DSS source result establishes that the original book was read or that its mechanism was tested here.

The linked DOI identifies Foot’s 2002 Virtues and Vices monograph, not the standalone 1967 Oxford Review article. Cite the intended article or specify the later collected edition. No guessed chapter/page or full-book reading is supplied.

The DOI identifies Kahneman/Tversky’s 1979 Econometrica 47(2) original, not a new 2018 study. The listed 2018 anthology may be a reprint, but should be cited consistently as such. Original/reprint are not independent studies, and this experiment did not fit a prospect-theory model.

Designing for Human-Centered Systems: Situational Risk as a Factor of Trust in Automation is HFES Annual Meeting 54(25):2130–2134, 2010, not 2012. Primary DOI metadata verifies identity; the full original was not read.

Both entries give the same authors, year and DOI 10.1207/S15327566IJCE0401_04. They are one source, not two independent scale validations. The local five-item adaptation and added negative wording require their own measurement interpretation.

The PDF and RWTH record explicitly state 8 October 2021 online publication; the journal issue is March 2022, 3(1):46–57. Preserve both dates and use one DOI/evidence identity. The filename’s 2022 is not an error requiring an invented new paper.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: If the quoted F tests and generalized eta squared refer to the conventional same-ANOVA decomposition, reported risk .88, reliability .88 and decision time .74 exceed partial eta squared bounds about .549, .792 and .342. Context .092 and interaction .05 do not. Original model/effect-size output is needed before assigning corrected generalized values. Printed F-test significance largely reconciles.

The actual rendered formula prints F(1.93,81,13), three values. 81.13 would match the expected corrected df pattern near 42 subject df, but is not verified original output. Preserve a likely formatting/transcription question, not a recovered exact statistic.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Gross/net payoffs and manual superiority, Figure2/p51
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Methods allow manual payoff 1.1 or .9 times rP, so nonautomation at 100% cannot automatically be classified as irrational. Figure2 also displays a negative failure amount; actual balance-debit rules and loss frequencies are unavailable. Distinguish success-weighted gross from net expectation without pretending the conditional illustration is implemented code.

Risk means average 53.8375%, reliability means 53.8133%, context means 53.8467%, versus reported overall 53.9%. Some differences exceed simple rounding for a fully balanced complete dataset. Missing observations, weighting or transcription need original output; do not replace the overall mean or infer broad data fabrication.

Postblock risk-perception label corresponds to willingness to take risk; pretrial risk propensity and theoretical probability/severity appraisal differ. DSS compliance is self-reported. Full item wording, code and model output are insufficient to treat these as independently validated latent mechanisms.

Caption attributes adaptation to [30,p36], but reference30 is listed pp1–12; reference31 is a risk review pp29–48. This is a locator/provenance mismatch. Originals not fully read, so no silent source substitution or assertion of the intended page.

methodological_limits: 43participants each give repeated fictional decisions;study uses repeated-measures analyses,not4644independent participants. Small convenience sample and unpaidgame limit population/real-world inference.
Riskcategories bundlewho/whatcanbeharmed,not a pure numericriskincrease. Higherproperty-onlydelegationprecludes a universalall-risk-reduces-useclaim.
Context can communicate relevant vulnerability or implicitstake differences. The authors acknowledge these unmeasured mental models;do not equate a contextual effect with irrational framing.
Taskchoices,reportedtrust,traitriskpropensity and appraised hazard are different. No unique psychological mediator or actual machine morality is measured.
Manual EVcanexceedstatedautomationEV;historical100%isnot a futureguarantee. Maximizinguseisnot a valid calibration criterion by itself.
Support-source nulls do not prove equivalence or uniquely verify a media-equation mechanism. Actual advicefollowing was not the displayedcompliance outcome.
Same-modelη²inconsistencies and ambiguouspayoffs require originaloutput. Conditional bounds and gross/net illustrations are not corrected authorresults or raw-data replication.
Authors report exemption,consent,voluntarywithdrawal and major task/context limitations. Do not allege hidden absence of ethics or universally concealedlimitations.
Currenthuman-factors evidence does not authorize clinical deployment,realharmexperiments,driverprofiling,newethicalprinciples or automatic harm links.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: 3×4×3×3=108 trials per person; 43×108=4644 planned decisions. Nine blocks of 12 trials are consistent. Repeated-measures F df84 and252 match 42×2 and42×6.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All reported ANOVA p-values are arithmetically wrong
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Displayed F values broadly reproduce thresholds, context p.011 and marginal p.078. Generalized eta squared labels require separate clarification; do not discard every inferential result.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Every contrast t126 or t84 must have paired-test df42
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Contrasts can use pooled repeated-measures error rather than a separate paired t-test. Without contrast/model output, these df are not automatically proof of ignored dependence.
Property-only delegation 72.78% exceeds no-risk 64.21%, while human/combined risks reduce use. Source categories are qualitatively different; do not force a universal numeric risk gradient.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Manual choice under100% reliability must be aversion
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Manual payoff can exceed automation expectation, and participants may not interpret past100% as a guarantee. The authors also acknowledge uncertain reasons. No universal optimality classification.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: A book-review DOI proves the book was read
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Reference69 DOI identifies a Martin review, not the Reeves/Nass book. Likewise, repeated Jian references are one original, and reprints do not add independent evidence.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Source choice and economic optimality differ. Do not infer aversion from less-than-maximal AI use without checking manual payoffs, comparative success beliefs and process values.

Read actual question wording and figures: trust/risk labels need not target the assumed latent construct. Preserve genuine nulls and conditional statistical questions instead of forcing positive findings.

deferred.term: Risk aversion/risk propensity as additional rows
deferred.reason: Pretrial risk disposition is measured, but the primary instrument and distinct preference construct are not fully reviewed here. Keep neutral risk appraisal distinct and avoid turning any safe choice into bias.

deferred.term: Moral deference from delegation of delivery
deferred.reason: Delegating execution with moral consequences is not necessarily accepting another agent’s moral judgment. No automatic mapping or new moral-outsourcing row.
No-risk still risks the automated agent, and choice rates do not show matching frequency as a strategy. High-reliability effects do not uniquely identify these mechanisms.

deferred.term: Media equation/CASA as a confirmed new mechanism
deferred.reason: Used as a post-hoc interpretation of a source-label null; no unique process measure, factorial test or full-book reading.
Reported unwillingness to trade human injury for fictional profit does not establish a distinct named doctrine, universal prohibition or threshold function.

limitations: One neutral risk-appraisal construct added; two existing concepts directly enriched and two receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes 819 in the same eleven categories. Source years, book/review/reprint identities, successful arithmetic and unresolved reporting issues remain explicit.
